name: Japan

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024: land area 364,500 km2 (World Bank AG.LND.TOTL.K2); high adds ~3% for inland water.

population.note: asOf 2025: 123,366,734 (World Bank). Range allows for 2026 change.

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2026 p.272 as quoted: 247,150 active. CIA Factbook 2025 230-240,000. Japan Coast Guard (14,800 paramilitary per IISS) excluded.

trainedReserves.note: IISS Military Balance 2026: 55,900 reserves (Ready Reserve and Reserve Personnel); low allows for the chronic Ready Reserve shortfall (educated).

supportPersonnel.note: Active 247,150 minus infantry P roles 47,000 = 200,150. Maritime SDF (~45,000), Air SDF (~47,000), GSDF artillery, armour, air-defence and logistics personnel, staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. No conscription since 1945; constitutional and demographic limits (median age ~49); 1% is ~1.2 million.

weapons.note: Anchor 10 minus: precision munitions, Type 12 upgraded standoff missiles, Tomahawk acquisition, SM-3/SM-6.

armor.note: Anchor 9-10: Type 10 with modular armour and C4I.

ships.note: Anchor 10: Aegis/BMD fleet, Taigei lithium-ion submarines, F-35B-capable Izumo.

fortification.note: Anchor 10: layered BMD (SM-3, PAC-3), hardened southwest-island bases being built.

logistics.note: Anchor 9-10: C-2, KC-46, sealift; dependent on ports and civilian RO-RO.

communications.note: Anchor 10: X-band DSN satellites, data links with US forces.

isr.note: Anchor 10: IGS reconnaissance satellites, E-2D/E-767, P-1, Global Hawk.

cyber.note: Anchor 10 minus: Cyber Defense Command (2022), active cyber defence law 2025.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP (2011 int$) 4,768,227,848,174 / population 123,366,734 = 38,651. Range +/-15%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 5,956,561,958,994 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 4,768,227,848,174 2011 int$. Range +/-15% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/JPN/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD?format=json Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 1.41% of GDP in 2025. Factbook: 1.4% (2024), 1% (2021). High allows for the 2% (incl. related spending) target for FY2027.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2024: industry incl. construction 26.8% of GDP (World Bank).

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Food self-sufficiency ~38% on a calorie basis; no surplus, heavily import-dependent.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 60,151,475 x share of males aged 15-19 4.842% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 582,468. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation.

armor.note: Educated guess. MHI Type 10 low-rate line. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Japan_Ground_Self-Defense_Force)

ifv_apc.note: Educated guess. Komatsu exit; Patria AMV licence production (Japan Steel Works). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Japan_Ground_Self-Defense_Force)

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. F-35A FACO (MHI Nagoya). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan_Air_Self-Defense_Force)

helicopters.note: Educated guess. Subaru UH-2, Kawasaki CH-47. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Japan_Ground_Self-Defense_Force)

ships_major.note: Educated guess. MHI, JMU shipyards: FFM 2/yr, ASEV. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_Japan_Maritime_Self-Defense_Force_ships)

submarines.note: Educated guess. One Taigei per year (MHI/KHI). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_Japan_Maritime_Self-Defense_Force_ships)

missiles.note: Educated guess. Type 12 launchers per year. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_equipment_of_the_Japan_Ground_Self-Defense_Force)

roadKm.note: asOf 2021: 1,218,772 km total, 992,835 km paved (mid), 30,469 km 4-lane+ (MLIT as quoted).

railKm.note: asOf 2011: 20,087 route-km (World Bank). World Bank value is from 2011 (JR network); CIA Factbook 27,311 km (2015, incl. private lines) as high.

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: 43,828 thousand DWT under the national flag. Range +/-10%. Japanese-owned fleet is far larger under flags of convenience (Panama).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Home-island defence with sea-lift to the southwest islands; little overseas sustainment experience.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 lists nine nuclear-armed states; Japan is not one of them.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: island geography, fortified bases and full population support.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with a 2026 order of battle. Population inside ne:JPN (World Bank 2025). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Counts from the Wikipedia JGSDF equipment list, JMSDF active-ship list and JASDF inventory table (grade B/C); the Japanese MoD Defense of Japan white paper was not fetched. ships_major includes the Izumo/Hyuga helicopter/F-35B carriers. US Forces Japan (~55,000) not included. Infantry splits, missile launchers and air-defence batteries are educated estimates. Japan Coast Guard excluded.
